Enumerate possible joint parent sets (joint-IDA)

Source: R/identification.R
possible_joint_parent_sets.Rd

Generalizes possible_parent_sets() from a single intervention node to a set xs of simultaneous interventions: every undirected edge incident to at least one node of xs is jointly reoriented, keeping only orientations that introduce no new v-structure and remain acyclic. Each returned entry is a list of parent sets in the same order as xs (entry i gives a valid parent set for xs[i] under that joint orientation).

Usage

possible_joint_parent_sets(cg, xs)

Arguments

cg

A PDAG-family (PDAG, CPDAG, MPDAG) graph created with cgraph().

xs

Character vector of node names (the simultaneous interventions; must be non-empty with no duplicates).

Value

List of lists of character vectors: one list per valid joint orientation, each containing one parent set per node of xs.

References

Maathuis MH, Kalisch M, Bühlmann P (2009). “Estimating high-dimensional intervention effects from observational data.” The Annals of Statistics, 37(6A), 3133–3164.

Nandy P, Maathuis MH, Richardson TS (2017). “Estimating the effect of joint interventions from observational data in sparse high-dimensional settings.” The Annals of Statistics, 45(2), 647–674.

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  cpdag <- cgraph(
    X1 %---% X2, X1 %---% A, X2 %---% B, A %-->% Y, B %-->% Y,
    class = "CPDAG"
  )
  possible_joint_parent_sets(cpdag, c("X1", "X2"))
}
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> [1] "X2"
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] "B"
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> [1] "A"
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> [1] "X1"
#> 
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [[3]][[1]]
#> character(0)
#> 
#> [[3]][[2]]
#> [1] "X1"
#> 
#>

#> [[4]][[1]]
